A second hamster (or part of one) is visible in the foreground, partially obscuring the main subject's lower body. The lighting is somewhat dim, and the image has a grainy quality typical of older digital cameras or high-ISO settings.

A single small, dark, bead-like eye is clearly visible on the side of the head, matching the species description.
One ear is clearly visible; it is rounded, relatively large compared to the head size, and positioned correctly. The inner ear structure shows pinkish skin, which is natural.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the body is round, compact, and stocky, fitting the 'potato' shape characteristic of hamsters.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The fur appears dense and short, with a golden/orange hue on the back and lighter cream/white on the underside. Texture looks consistent with real fur, despite image noise.

The rear of the hamster is either cut off by the frame or obscured by the foreground subject/bedding. The tail is not visible.

The boundary where the main hamster overlaps with the foreground hamster is soft and slightly indistinct due to depth of field and image quality, but no clear 'melting' or fusion of anatomy is evident. It appears to be two separate animals.
